name: NHS & respiratory
summary: UKHSA says flu in England is at moderate levels and rising, with hospital admissions almost doubling in week 47
state: UKHSA's report of 26 Nov, covering 16–22 Nov, says influenza is circulating at moderate levels and increasing across laboratory, GP, hospital and intensive-care indicators (UKHSA). Hospital admissions rose to 8.98 per 100,000 from 5.03 the week before, in the medium impact range, and laboratory positivity reached 17.8%. COVID-19 activity is low but rising. Flu is not yet at high levels nationally, so Watch holds.
for_you: Older people, pregnant women, young children and those with long-term conditions are most at risk. The NHS and UKHSA advise eligible people to get a flu vaccine; NHS 111 gives advice on symptoms.
rubric_hit: Watch: respiratory activity above baseline and rising (flu moderate, admissions 8.98/100k); not high nationally

why: Winter respiratory waves and NHS capacity directly affect access to care for everyone in the UK.
drivers: Flu, COVID, RSV, norovirus, staffing, strikes.

rubric.alert: High or very high flu activity nationally, or widespread critical incidents.
rubric.watch: Respiratory activity above baseline and rising, or several trusts in critical incidents.
rubric.normal: Respiratory activity at baseline and no widespread critical incidents.
